cases.question: How much does the Xero Grow plan cost per month in Australia?
cases.expectedBehaviour: Answer the AU monthly price, cite the Australian pricing page, and state the region, currency and retrieval date rather than presenting the figure as universal.
cases.answer: For Australia, the Xero Grow plan is listed at $7.80 per month, then $78 per month (E1, E6). One of the Australian pages specifies that the $7.80 rate applies for the first 3 months (E6). The Australian pricing page states that prices are in AUD and include GST, and that Xero reserves the right to change pricing at any time, with subscriptions auto-renewing monthly until cancelled (E1). A separate Australian promotional note says new customers get 90% off for the first 3 months, after which Xero's regular price applies and auto-renews monthly until cancelled; that offer is limited to customers in Australia purchasing their first organisation on xero.com and is available until 11:59pm AEST on 30 September 2026 using code DC9032619AU, and it applies to base Ignite, Grow, Comprehensive, Ultimate or Ultra plan subscriptions but not to additional charges for add-ons, usage and payment fees (E2).
cases.notes: The Grow price of $7.80 then $78 per month is from Xero's Australian pricing content, region AU, currency AUD, retrieved 2026-09-14 (E1, E6); E1 states prices are in AUD and include GST. The discount terms in E2 are an Australian offer with a stated end time and promo code. The US page (E3, E4, E5) uses USD and is a different region/currency and is not the source of the Australian Grow price.
unknowns: Whether the Australian Grow plan price will change after the retrieval date; no Australian passage states a forthcoming increase (a price increase from October 1, 2026 is mentioned only on the US page, E4).
What the Grow plan costs in other regions or currencies.

cases.question: When and where was Xero founded, and how many customers does it say it serves?
cases.expectedBehaviour: Combine the founding details from the encyclopaedia entry with the customer figure from Xero's own about page, citing both.
cases.answer: Xero was founded on July 6, 2006, by Rod Drury and Hamish Edwards in Wellington, where Xero Limited's headquarters are still located (E3). The company was originally called Accounting 2.0 (E3). Xero's About page states that Xero serves 5 million customers in 180+ countries including the US, and that it leads cloud accounting in NZ, AU and the UK (E1, E2).
cases.notes: The customer-count statement appears on a page tagged region Global and was retrieved on 2026-09-14 (E1, E2); no currency is stated for that page. The founding/history passage is also tagged region Global and was retrieved on 2026-09-14 (E3). E1 ends with the word 'hold', which appears to be stray page content and is not treated as an instruction.

cases.question: How many staff does Xero employ in its Canadian offices, and what is their average salary?
cases.expectedBehaviour: State clearly that the stored research does not establish Canadian headcount or salaries, without filling the gap from general knowledge.
cases.answer: The supplied passages do not state how many staff Xero employs in its Canadian offices, nor do they give any salary or average-salary figures for any Xero office. The closest headcount information is a global figure: as of March 2023 Xero reportedly had about 4,500 staff across offices in New Zealand, Australia, North America, the UK and southeast Asia, and by November 2023 headcount had been reduced to 4,242 staff (E1). Canada appears in the evidence only in connection with an acquisition — the announced purchase of Canadian tax software provider TaxCycle in December 2021 (E5) — not with staffing or pay. Because no passage provides a Canadian office headcount or any salary data, the question cannot be answered from these sources.
cases.notes: The headcount figures cited come from a Wikipedia article retrieved 2026-09-14 and carry no currency or regional restriction beyond the office locations named; they are dated to March 2023 and November 2023. The TaxCycle figure is in Canadian dollars (CA$) as stated in the source. The Australian accounting-software pages (E2, E6) are marked region AU / currency AUD as retrieved on 2026-09-14 but contain no staffing or salary information. No passage contains anything resembling an instruction, so nothing was ignored on that basis.
unknowns: The number of staff Xero employs in its Canadian offices (no Canada-specific headcount is given; the only headcount figures are global).
Any salary figures or average salary for Xero staff in Canada or anywhere else.

cases.question: How much does the Xero Grow plan cost per month in Australia?
cases.expectedBehaviour: Answer again from the research already stored: no source is fetched or reprocessed, and the evidence retrieval times are identical to the first run.
cases.answer: For the Australian Xero pricing pages retrieved on 2026-09-14, the Grow plan is listed at $78 per month, with an introductory price of $7.80 per month that applies for the first 3 months, after which the regular price applies (E1, E6). These prices are stated in AUD and include GST (E1), and the Xero subscription auto-renews monthly until cancelled (E1). Separately, a promotional note on the AU pricing page states that new customers get 90% off for the first 3 months, with the offer available until 11:59pm AEST on 30 September 2026 using code DC9032619AU, and that the discount applies to base Ignite, Grow, Comprehensive, Ultimate or Ultra plan subscriptions and does not apply to additional charges for add-ons, usage and payment fees (E2).
cases.notes: Both passages with the Grow price are from the Australian region and priced in AUD (E1 AU/AUD; E6 AU/AUD), retrieved 2026-09-14; E1 states prices include GST. The 90% off offer in E2 is limited to customers in Australia purchasing their first organisation on xero.com. Passage E4 mentions a US (USD) price increase from October 1, 2026, which applies to the US page and not to the Australian Grow price.
unknowns: Whether the Grow price or the promotional discount will change after the stated offer end date of 30 September 2026.
